summary: Independently re-verified iteration 16's blocked-user exclusion feature end-to-end. Backend: 4/4 pytest tests passed -- GET /api/bot/status blocked_users count matches direct DB count_documents({blocked:True}); POST /api/admin/broadcast's upfront `total` correctly excludes blocked users (58 total, 18 pre-existing blocked -> total=40, matching main agent's own numbers exactly); ran two consecutive broadcasts confirming totals stay consistent and regression invariants (sent+failed==total, sum(error_counts)==failed) hold (both completed sent=40/failed=0/error_counts={} since remaining 40 users are real/deliverable); verified track()'s un-block-on-interact by simulating a webhook /start from a currently-blocked user_id -- confirmed track() runs before reply() in on_start (so the fake/undeliverable chat's reply_text failure, if any, doesn't block the DB update) and the user's blocked field flipped from true to false in db.bot_users, dropping blocked_users from 18 to 17. Frontend: unlocked panel with PIN 246810, confirmed 'unique users' Cell (stat-users) renders the new sub-label '17 blocked' directly under the '58' count, matching the live blocked_users value from /api/bot/status -- clean rendering, correct contrast, no layout issues.
critical_code_review_comments: _mark_blocked() is called from both the first-upload path and the main batch loop in run_broadcast_job(), correctly scoped to only 'blocked_bot' and 'invalid_chat' categories (not rate_limited/network_timeout/other, which are transient and shouldn't permanently exclude a user) -- correct judgment call.

track()'s $set of blocked: False on every interaction is a clean, simple self-healing mechanism; on_start calls track() before reply(), so un-blocking is not dependent on the reply actually succeeding -- confirmed via live webhook simulation with a non-deliverable chat id (webhook still returned 200 and the DB update completed).

run_broadcast_job()'s all_user_ids query now filters blocked:{$ne:true} consistently with server.py's total count -- both use the same filter shape, so the upfront total the admin sees before queuing matches what the job will actually attempt.

Minor observation (not a bug): GET /api/bot/status's unique_users field still counts ALL bot_users including blocked ones, while blocked_users is a separate count -- this is correct/expected since the frontend combines both (58 total, 17 blocked as sub-label) rather than subtracting them, and this matches the intended UX of showing total reach vs. currently-reachable.
No bugs found. Clean, minimal, additive change; correctly reuses the existing error-categorization from iteration 15 to decide what counts as a permanent block vs a transient failure.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (sub-label rendering verified against live status API)

seed_data_creation: 2 additional TEST_-prefixed broadcasts sent to the 40 currently-unblocked preview users during pytest (both completed sent=40/failed=0), plus 1 synthetic webhook /start simulating a blocked user id 5924401094 re-interacting (which un-blocked them, dropping db blocked count from 18 to 17).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 16's blocked-user exclusion + un-block-on-interact feature is fully verified end-to-end (backend invariants, DB state transitions, and frontend sub-label). Current preview state: 58 total bot_users, 17 blocked (was 18 before this test run's un-block verification), 41 not blocked -- reflects real state after this session's tests, not a fresh reset. No bugs found across iterations 14, 15, 16 (resumable jobs, error diagnostics, blocked exclusion all compose correctly together).
rca of the issue: N/A -- no bugs found this iteration; the original problem (broadcasts wasting attempts on users who blocked the bot) is resolved by _mark_blocked() + the blocked:{$ne:true} filter in both the broadcast query and the upfront total count, with automatic self-healing via track()'s blocked:False reset on any subsequent interaction.
